steps.title: Explore the filesystem
steps.description: Get familiar with your sandbox environment. Find out where you are, and explore the directory structure.
tasks: Run `pwd` to see your current directory
Run `ls -la` to see all files (including hidden ones)
Navigate to `/` and list the top-level directories

steps.title: Create a project structure
steps.description: Build a web project directory structure from scratch using mkdir and touch.
tasks: Create a directory called `webapp` in your home directory

verification.command: test -d /home/student/webapp/src && test -d /home/student/webapp/public && test -d /home/student/webapp/config && test -f /home/student/webapp/src/index.js && test -f /home/student/webapp/public/index.html && test -f /home/student/webapp/config/app.conf && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: Write and read file content
steps.description: Use echo and cat to write content to files and read them back.
tasks: Write a valid HTML page into `public/index.html` with an `<h1>` tag
Use `cat` to verify both files have content

verification.command: grep -q '<h1>' /home/student/webapp/public/index.html && grep -q 'console.log' /home/student/webapp/src/index.js && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: File permissions challenge
steps.description: Make your JavaScript file executable and restrict config file access.

verification.command: test -x /home/student/webapp/src/index.js && stat -c '%a' /home/student/webapp/config/app.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -q '444' && echo PASS || (stat -f '%Lp' /home/student/webapp/config/app.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -q '444' && test -x /home/student/webapp/src/index.js && echo PASS || echo FAIL)

steps.title: Process investigation
steps.description: Explore running processes in your sandbox environment.
tasks: List all running processes with `ps aux`
Find the PID of your shell process
Start a background process with `sleep 300 &`, then find it with `ps` and kill it

verification.command: ps aux | grep -v grep | grep -c '' | awk '{if ($1 > 0) print "PASS"; else print "FAIL"}'
